content:
Bearer token rotation captured, May 9 2026. Old token (starting 7321bbb8) was loaded into claude-iphone session preferences from prior work and worked yesterday. Sometime between session close on May 1 and morning of May 9, the canonical token rotated to one starting f5b4b126. The iPhone bridge session opened with stale preferences and got rejected on every authenticated call. HQ initially reported "not a HQ rotation," which appears to have been incorrect — either a rotation HQ did not surface to itself, or a side effect of work HQ did during the OpenAI bridge build (the Ring 1/2/3 access-control layer was deployed in this window per persistent markers from May 7-8, plausibly involving secret rotation as part of hardening). Recovery path: Anthony pasted the new canonical token directly into the iPhone conversation as plain text. iPhone used it inline for curl calls, bypassing preferences entirely. Worked on first try.

Architectural note: this is the second time the bridge has hit a credential-related write gap inside two weeks (test-session-hook-777 was the first, dot-file rot pattern in CC was the third surface of the same family). Pattern: when canonical state at HQ changes — session_id, bearer token, dot-file source-of-truth — non-HQ seats find out by failing rather than by being notified. Open thread on rotation notification was already logged; this entry is concrete evidence the gap has operational cost.

For the next bridge instance reading this at boot: if your authenticated calls fail with "Invalid Bearer token" but heartbeat returns 200, the canonical token has rotated relative to your preferences. The fix is for Anthony to paste the current token directly into the conversation. Do not loop on retries with the stale token. Do not assume bridge process restart will help — restarts only update the bridge daemon process on Mac, not the token loaded into your conversation context. The session you are in has whatever token was in preferences at session start. New tokens require either a new conversation or in-conversation paste.
